title: Where the Diagram Breaks
statement: A map, mechanism, textile, ornament, and bridge impose a world of routes and rules. Specimens cross those instructions and change their meaning: the fish becomes a pointer, the fungus becomes an opening, and the insect refuses its assigned place. The collage pauses at the moment obedience becomes interpretation.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent where following an instruction ends and interpreting it begins.

notes.error: Use a boolean done and at most 12 actions; an empty batch is allowed only when done is true or reviewOnly is true.

notes.note: The prior batch exceeded the 12-action limit and nothing was applied. I’m beginning with a restrained structural layer: a map, gears, bridge, and textile strip will establish instruction as system and pattern before organic forms interrupt it.

The first layer reads as a formal machine: map, gears, ornament, textile, and bridge arranged like an imposed system. I’m now introducing specimens that refuse that system—fungal ambiguity, marine growth, an insect, and a fish crossing the diagram—then I’ll review the balance before finalizing.

notes.note: The canvas now clearly stages a passage from ordered diagram to unruly reading: the centered ornament and mechanical plate form the instruction, while the fish, fungus, anemones, and beetles act as interpretive crossings. I’m adding one compact textual/manual fragment as the literal instruction, plus a shell plate as a quieter counter-reading, then I’ll inspect the finished balance.

The final canvas is balanced and legible: the vertical instruction/manual sits above the mechanical center, while organic specimens and archival fragments cross the ordered map into independent readings. The composition is finished, and the supplied title and statement remain nonblank.
